messages.author: fd1045e5e460f32a
messages.subject: overlay histogram and density line
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to generate a plot using qplot, and I am wondering anybody can help my questions below.

 

The first plot (attached pdf) is created by:

qplot(FAQTOTAL,..density..,data=d, geom="histogram", binwidth=2, xlab="FAQ") + facet_grid(BASECLASS~VISIT)

 

  1. how I can add density line overlay with histogram, as shown in the bottom plot (created by lattice)?
  2. how I can change x-axis to “0”, “10”,” 20”,”30”? Current x-axis is too crowded….
  3. y-label (“density”) is too close to the y axis. Can I move it a little bit to the left?
  4. Can I change the histogram color (currently dark gray) to other color (such as white)?

 

I just started use ggplot and some questions are probably naïve…..but I appreciate your help.

Thank you,

Kaori

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: overlay histogram and density line
parts: Hi,

On Mon, Mar 21, 2011 at 12:02 AM, Ito, Kaori (New London/PGRD)
<Kaor...@pfizer.com> wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I am trying to generate a plot using qplot, and I am wondering anybody can
> help my questions below.
>
>
>
> The first plot (attached pdf) is created by:
>
> qplot(FAQTOTAL,..density..,data=d, geom="histogram", binwidth=2, xlab="FAQ")
> + facet_grid(BASECLASS~VISIT)
>
>
>
> how I can add density line overlay with histogram, as shown in the bottom
> plot (created by lattice)?
+ geom_density()

> how I can change x-axis to “0”, “10”,” 20”,”30”? Current x-axis is too
> crowded….
+ scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(0,10,20,30))

> y-label (“density”) is too close to the y axis. Can I move it a little bit
> to the left?
+ scale_y_continuous("density\n")

> Can I change the histogram color (currently dark gray) to other color (such
> as white)?
Use fill=I("white") inside the qplot call.

>
>
>
> I just started use ggplot and some questions are probably naïve…..but I
> appreciate your help.

HTH,
Ista

>
> Thank you,
>
> Kaori

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: overlay histogram and density line
parts:
+ ylim(0,1)

or

coord_cartisian(ylim=c(0,1))

The first way will throw away data not within the limit (although this
should not be a problem in your case because you want to extend rather
than restrinct the range), the second just "zooms in".

Best,
Ista
